dropped_paths_reasons.OpenMW-CS editor: apps/opencs/, apps/opencs_tests/, files/opencs/, docs/source/manuals/openmw-cs/, files/mac/openmw-cs*, files/openmw-cs.cfg and files/org.openmw.cs.desktop: the fork has no content editor, and none of these exist in it
dropped_paths_reasons.Morrowind installation wizard: apps/wizard/, files/wizard/, files/lang/wizard_*.ts, extern/osgQt/, cmake/FindLIBUNSHIELD.cmake and cmake/FindTinyXML.cmake: the wizard installs Morrowind from a disc and is the only user of these libraries
dropped_paths_reasons.Morrowind importers: apps/essimporter/ (Morrowind saves), apps/mwiniimporter/ (Morrowind.ini) and the launcher's import page (apps/launcher/importpage.*, apps/launcher/ui/importpage.ui): the fork reads Fallout files
dropped_paths_reasons.Morrowind-only tools: apps/navmeshtool/, components/navmeshtool/, apps/bulletobjecttool/: command line tools the fork does not build; apps/openmw/mwscript/docs/ is the manual of Morrowind's script language
dropped_paths_reasons.Windows: files/windows/ and the Windows-only sources (crash catcher, path helpers, windows.hpp, the Win32 file backend, platform.* which only raises the file handle limit on Windows): the fork is macOS-only (floor macOS 26, Apple Silicon)
dropped_paths_reasons.Android and Linux: androidmain.cpp, androidpath.*, gl4esinit.* (gl4es is a GLES wrapper for Android), linuxpath.*, the Linux desktop entries and appdata file: the fork is macOS-only
dropped_paths_reasons.Upstream's packaging and test scaffoldin: docker/, manual/ (upstream's documentation build), scripts/data/ and scripts/integration_tests.py (integration tests that need Morrowind data), scripts/preprocessed_file_size_stats*.py (used only by upstream's GitLab CI)
dropped_paths_reasons.Upstream's own CI and hosting files: .github/ (the fork has its own workflows, and the sync job's token may not push changes to workflow files), .gitlab-ci.yml, .gitlab/, CI/ (the fork's own scripts live there), README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md (the fork has its own); CHANGELOG.md is the list of what OpenMW's releases fix, and it names fixes whose merge requests the fork did not take, so taking it would describe a tree the fork does not have
